rationale: newjordan's promoted harness (PR #233, main's submission/ at d0929e6) is in this package twice. labs/plain and labs/overseer are its plain/ and overseer/ byte for byte, with no change of ours, and play the four lab tasks. plain/, overseer/ and tests/ at the root are the same code with changes of ours that the note describes (a released lockdown orders workshops on the surface so that DF rebuilds its path index, and the wood-tool orders pause meanwhile; the loop tries a failing read again instead of exiting), and play the fresh embark (OP1). The shared dfbench_client/ is main's. Everything else it does in those games is its own work and that of the sources its declaration lists (our PR #124's tree and its lineage among them).

One more change of ours is in the root tree, marked `h5`: overseer/openplay.py (reconnect: past the game's allowance of release-guard workshops a release may order one more when none is waiting) and its test in tests/test_h2_reconnect.py. A second `h5` change in the root tree is in overseer/openplay.py (cull: a hunger check that marks nothing starts no cooldown), with its test in tests/test_winner_fixes.py. A third `h5` change in the root tree is in overseer/harness.py (defend: a nearest-hostile distance of 0 is a hostile on the wagon's tile, and a refused warning is tried again the next day), with its test in tests/test_h2_reconnect.py. Overseer.meeting_area, which our packages from PR #240 to PR #249 had changed so that no underground meeting area was made on OP1, is main's rule again in this package (its docstring says so, marked `h5`; tests/test_winner_fixes.py has main's expectation back).

rationale: yukonautominer's published harness (PR #168) starts the hunger cull's cooldown only when the pass marked an animal: a check that found nothing it may slaughter (every animal left kept for the feast) used to start it too, so a food-zero emergency days later waited out the 5 or 8 days. This package makes the same one-line change in its own cull() on the open tasks (the lab tasks never reach it); the comment there credits them. In 366 of our local games the old rule held back such a cull in 18, inside the scored last 28 days in 7. In this package that code is in ours/, the controller for the handed-over fort (MY1), as in our e884d63b.

rationale: yukonautominer's published harness (PR #178) builds a strange mood's workshop again when the listed one has stood with its construction suspended: its mood() reads the controller's own shops(), which leaves such a workshop out, where the leader's code read the raw workshop list and waited on it for good. The same harness cancels the controller's own standing wood-crafts order once created wealth reaches the target (first in their PR #165, 11ff6d2a, declared in its own entry): the leader's code only stopped adding the order, so three crafts a day were made to the end of the game. This package makes both changes in its own mood() and progression_push(); the comments there credit them. The cancel here is final once the game accepts it. In this package that code is in ours/, the controller for the handed-over fort (MY1), as in our e884d63b.
